newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks end mixed, blue chips backtrack.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks end mixed, blue chips backtrack.

text.p: Profit-taking sent Kuala Lumpur blue chips into negative territory after two days of post-festival gains, but interest perked up in the small-capitalisation sector.
The Composite Index ended off 12.19 points or 0.97 percent to 1,246.91. "It's a rotation play," said an institutional dealer. "I suppose the index was not helped by (weakness in) Telekom and Tenaga."
Wall Street's gain of 60 points provided little help. "I don't know if sentiment from Hong Kong affected us," the dealer said, referring to the drop in that bourse.
The Second Board index, which had been lagging blue chips, regained momentum to rise 9.64 points to 627.82.
Volume eased to 441 million shares from 589 million.
Stocks were down most of the session, with the selloff in the Composite Index accelerating at day's end.

"The run-up in the market is very selective," said Patrick Zecha, head of research at South Johor Securities. For his part, he said he is still positive on motor stocks "even though the prices have run up".
A weakening yen and stronger ringgit bode well for the earnings of automakers, analysts say.
